content.text: Kaluki (also spelled Kalooki or Kalookie) is a popular rummy variant played throughout Europe and North America. Using two standard decks plus Jokers, players aim to meld all their cards through sets and runs. The defining feature is the initial meld requirementâ€”typically 40 or 51 pointsâ€”which must be met before a player can lay down any cards. The game rewards careful hand management and the strategic use of Jokers.

Kaluki emerged in the mid-20th century as an evolution of standard rummy games, likely developing simultaneously in British and North American card clubs. The name 'Kalooki' may derive from Eastern European Jewish communities who popularized the game in London and New York.
Two standard 52-card decks plus 2 Jokers (106 cards total). Cards rank A-K-Q-J-10-9-8-7-6-5-4-3-2 with Aces high only.
Standard cards, score sheet, chips or counters for stakes (optional)
Each player receives 13 cards dealt singly. The next card is turned face-up to start the discard pile; remaining cards form the stock.

items.text: Kalooki 40 (British): Initial meld requirement is 40 points instead of 51. More common in British clubs and faster-paced.
Kalooki 51 (North American): Standard North American version requiring 51-point initial meld. More strategic and defensive.
Swedish Kalooki: Variant with different Joker rules and sometimes three Jokers used. Scoring may vary.
Duplicate Cards Variant: Some house rules allow duplicate cards in sets (e.g., two 7 of Hearts from different decks). Must be agreed before play.
